subject: Helium AI: promptset A/B quality regression — parachute coordination
messages:
From: Bethany Cho <bethany.cho@helium.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 1 Jul 2029 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: sudden drop in promptset A (A/B) — examples attached

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing a consistent degradation in our customer-facing assistant when the team flipped to the new promptset A as part of our canary yesterday. The failure modes are short, mostly hallucination-like confabulations on price-related queries and a subtle tone shift that confuses the flow. 10 sample transcripts attached.

Can you please confirm whether Redwood rolled any runtime change (quant profile / kernel switch / routing) on our host yesterday afternoon? Our ops team flagged a P95 latency bump too but main customer impact is quality.

We'd like an ETA on mitigation and whether you can flip us back to the previous promptset variant while you investigate. This is impacting a small but growing set of trial users.

Thanks — Bethany
Bethany Cho
Head of Product Ops | Helium AI

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Bethany Cho <bethany.cho@helium.ai>, Helium AI Ops <ops@helium.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 1 Jul 2029 09:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden drop in promptset A (A/B) — examples attached

Bethany — thanks for the report and examples. I pulled the early canary logs and there were no infra-level kernel changes for your tenant between 16:00–19:00 PDT yesterday. We did push a promptset revision at 15:40 that changed a handful of instruction tokens (labelled promptset-A.v3).

Immediate plan:
- I'm opening an internal coordination thread (below) to propose a short "parachute" (safe rollback) so we can switch you back to promptset-A.v2 while we triage.
- Karthik / Marissa / Grace — can you prioritize an assessment of A/B metrics (utility, hallucination false positives, top-token divergence) on the v3 -> v2 comparison? If we can confirm a quality delta that crosses our acceptance gates we should flip at once.

Bethany — we aim to propose a rollback or a traffic-split plan within 4 hours. Can you confirm whether you want a full rollback or a 90/10 split for the next 24 hours?

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 1 Jul 2029 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden drop in promptset A (A/B) — examples attached

Quick triage notes:
- I ran the evaluation harness against the 500-sample metric set and saw a 1.9% mean utility drop (v3 vs v2) and hallucination-tagged responses up from 1.1% to 3.4%. Latency P95 rose ~60ms which could explain the ops flags.
- Acceptance gates (proposal): mean utility delta <= 0.5%, hallucination rate < 2.0%, semantic similarity (embedding cosine) >= 0.92 on canonical questions, P95 latency < 250ms.

Proposed immediate action:
1) Apply a 24-hour parachute: traffic -> promptset-A.v2 for 100% for Helium AI tenant.
2) Snapshot logs + install additional tracing hooks to collect token-level divergence for deeper root cause.
3) Postmortem to include prompt diff, model variant (q4b vs q8), quantization profile, and recent runtime kernel picks.

I'll attach a short metrics dump after the run. If everyone agrees, I can enact the rollback (ops-approved route) — need final OK from Kimberly and Grace.

—Karthik

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Jul 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden drop in promptset A (A/B) — examples attached

Adding details from the eval team and attaching the canary metrics (parachute_playbook_v1.pdf and canary-metrics-20290702.csv attached). Highlights:
- The regression is concentrated on price-entity prompts and conditional completion correctness. Automated NLI-based checks flagged divergent assertions in 12% of price queries.
- Model artifact differences: v3 included a tokenizer tweak and a soft-instruction weight change; those look likely culprits.

I support a 100% rollback to v2 for 24 hours while we do an A/B run with a reduced instruction set (v3-lite). Also recommending we add two quick acceptance checks to the console as guardrails: (1) "price-entity delta check" that compares grounding against canonical table; (2) automated hallucination detector on the canary channel.

I've uploaded the proposal to Drive and created JIRA INF-9723 for the remediation tasks.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Staff Applied ML Engineer, Eval & Quality

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Jul 2029 11:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden drop in promptset A (A/B) — parachute coordination

Ops note: we can trigger tenant-scoped rollbacks without a full deployment window. Key constraints:
- Rolling back to v2 will require an immediate routing update and a small capacity resync that could cause a transient 50–100ms spike for a few minutes.
- If we do 100% rollback, SLO will be restored for quality but we'll monitor for any infra-side latency impact.

I'll standby to execute the rollback once Kimberly confirms Helium's preference. Also recommending a short canary (1 hour) after rollback to validate stability before we mark the incident resolved.

Grace O'Connor
Senior SRE, Runtime

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Bethany Cho <bethany.cho@helium.ai>, Helium AI Ops <ops@helium.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 8 Jul 2029 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden drop in promptset A (A/B) — parachute coordination

Bethany — based on the eval and SRE readouts we will proceed with a full 24-hour rollback to promptset-A.v2 for your tenant. Grace will execute the tenant-scoped routing change shortly; expect a brief transient latency bump during the switch. Karthik and Marissa will collect additional traces and run the v3-lite experiments in parallel; JIRA INF-9723 tracks the work.

Action owners:
- Grace: execute rollback + 1h canary validation (ETA: 30m).
- Karthik: token-level divergence traces + metric summary (ETA: 6h).
- Marissa: follow-up A/B with v3-lite and add the two guardrail checks to the console prototype (ETA: 48h).
- Kimberly: liaison with Helium and monitor customer impact; prepare customer note once canary finishes.

Bethany — do you prefer we proceed with the rollback now? If yes, we'll start the route change and keep you on a tight update cadence.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
